layout.title: Documentation
layout.starterDescription: A production-ready baseline for teams that want a clean Nuxt foundation, not a demo shell.

hero.title: A practical guide to the Nuxt starter
hero.description: Learn how the starter is structured, how the pieces fit together, and how to build features without fighting the foundation.

overview.title: What this starter is for
overview.description: A clean base for production Nuxt apps with typed data flow, modular features, and predictable route shells.

service.title: Service-first API access
service.description: Call useApi() from feature services, keep transport details out of components, and make requests easy to test.

forms.title: Typed forms
forms.description: Use vee-validate and zod together so validation, submit state, and form values stay explicit.

layouts.title: Purposeful layouts
layouts.description: Use default for the app shell, auth for sign-in flows, docs for guidance, and blank for embeds or print views.

i18n.title: Locale-aware content
i18n.description: Shared and module strings are merged so English and Arabic stay aligned across the starter.

gettingStarted.title: Getting started
gettingStarted.description: Set up the starter conventions, confirm the theme, and build your first page with the right defaults.
gettingStarted.pageTitle: Build from the starter with clear, production-safe defaults.
gettingStarted.pageDescription: Start with the existing shell, keep service calls inside module services, and treat the docs as the source of truth for the starter's conventions.

layout.title: Read the layout contract
layout.description: Confirm which pages use the default shell, which use docs, and which should stay blank.

meta.title: Keep page metadata explicit
meta.description: Every page should define a title so route intent stays visible in code and navigation.

routes.title: 1. Confirm routes
routes.description: Decide whether a page belongs in the public shell, docs shell, auth shell, or blank shell before you build it.

services.title: 2. Use feature services
services.description: Wrap API requests with module services so views only handle presentation and interaction.

locale.title: 3. Keep copy localized
locale.description: Put UI strings in locale files so English and Arabic stay in sync as the project grows.

architecture.title: Architecture
architecture.description: Understand where shared logic lives, where feature logic belongs, and how the routes are composed.
architecture.pageTitle: The codebase is split by ownership, not by convenience.
architecture.pageDescription: Shared utilities stay in core, feature logic stays inside modules, pages compose the routes, and layouts define the shell behavior.

keepStable.title: What to keep stable
keepStable.description: The starter is strongest when the public shell stays simple, API access stays service-first, and the docs explain the conventions instead of duplicating them.

core.title: app/core
core.description: Shared helpers, API client, config, utilities, and app-wide composables.

modules.title: app/modules
modules.description: Feature ownership for pages, services, types, and component-level UI.

pages.title: app/pages
pages.description: Public routes for landing, docs, and product-facing entry points.

layouts.title: app/layouts
layouts.description: Shells that define the public, docs, auth, and blank experiences.

usage.title: How to use the starter
usage.description: Practical patterns for service calls, route metadata, auth, theming, and locale-safe UI.
usage.pageTitle: The practical rules for shipping features in this starter.
usage.pageDescription: These are the conventions that keep the codebase coherent as teams add more routes, forms, and API-driven screens.
usage.cta: Open the architecture guide for the full structure.

api.title: API access
api.description: Wrap all data access in feature services that use useApi().

meta.title: Page metadata
meta.description: Set definePageMeta on every page so titles and middleware stay explicit.

auth.title: Route protection
auth.description: Protect routes at the page level instead of hiding state behind global behavior.

locale.title: Locale text
locale.description: Keep user-facing text in locale files so the same route works in every supported language.
